newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sidel falls on H1 results, downgrades.
newsitem.headline: Sidel falls on H1 results, downgrades.

text.p: Shares in Sidel were down more than three percent in midday trading on Tuesday after the company which specialises in bottling machinery reported a 47 percent fall in first-half profit to 108 million francs.
Traders said several analysts cut their earnings forecasts for the group after the weaker-than-expected results.

Paribas Capital Markets, voicing concern about margin erosion, cut its rating on the share to hold from buy and lowered its earnings forecast to 10.20 francs per share for 1996 from 10.90. Cheuvreux de Virieu cut its EPS forecast 9.40 francs from 11.30 for 1996 and to 13 francs from 13.5 for 1997.
Sidel shares were down 10.10 francs at 309.90 at 1135 GMT.

"There was a big deterioration in terms of geographic mix," said an analyst who also cut his EPS forecast to 9.70 francs from 10.40 for 1996. "There was no recovery in orders in the United States. There are signs of a rebound in the Middle East, Afria and Europe but those are activities with thinner margins."

Sidel, which said it was penalised by high plastic prices, predicted its second-half turnover would exceed that of the first half for a full year total of more than three billion francs, compared with 3.7 billion for 1995. Its said turnover should rise in all regions except the Americas.
